2. Collector of Khulna on 16.5.59 made a reference to the Alluvial Lands Act, 1920 stating that some island chars were formed in the bed of the river Kazibacha in Mouza Tetultala within PS Batiaghata in the District of Khulna, as depicted in the sketch-map attached to the letter of reference, which had been shown as blocks 1-5 and 6-7 as prepared by khas mahals Surveyor and the chars comprising of 129.22 acres of cultivable land were being claimed by different persons including the government with the result that there were occasions for breach of peace. It was further stated that the Collector of Khulna therefore, attached the said char land in accordance with the provision of section 3 of the aforesaid Act and had appointed District Manager as receiver for management of the said land. The land were still under attachment and in possession of the receiver. As the Collector thought that rival claims of title and possession of this char land were likely to cause further breach of peace he referred the matter to the District Judge, Khulna for determining the claims of the different claimants. The District Judge under sub-section (2) of section 5 of the said Act transferred the reference to the Court of Subordinate Judge, Khulna where it was registered as Title Suit No. 5 of 1959. In the letter of reference 11 persons including the government were shown as persons claiming title and possession over the disputed land. However, after service of notice under section 5 of the said Act by the Court 40 more persons entered appearance and set up claims over the disputed land. They were added as defendant Nos. 12-51 in the suit. 

 4. Claimant Nos. 2-51 have been treated by the trial Court as defendants in the suit and for the sake of convenience we shall also term them as such. Defendant No. 2 Abdul Haque Sarder claims that during CS operation it was found that the river Kazibacha, which is also known as Ramdashia, flowed through Mouza Tetultala comprised in the permanent settlement estate of Touzi No. 120 of Khulna Collectorate and as such the settlement authority treated the former bed of the river as Diara land. Accordingly a Diara proceeding was started, and in the CS maps (sheet Nos. 1-3) prepared in 1922-23 this diara land was demarcated and a new Touzi No. 1144 was assigned to it. The land of these diara Touzi was taken in settlement by the proprietors of Touzi No. 120. The further case of defendant No. 2 is that river Kazibacha formerly flowed by the north-south and eastern sides of Mouza Tetultala but subsequently it receded on the north and south as a result of which there was gradual and imperceptible accretion to the land of Touzi Nos. 120 and 1140. In 1940 the Government again surveyed the land of Touzi No. 1140. Along with land accreted to this touzi were delineated in the map so prepared and separate khatians were opened in the names of those who were holding the land contiguous to their Asli land. But there was no survey of the land accreted to Touzi No. 120. However, the landlords brought suits against the tenants who were holding the land in Touzi No. 120 for increase of rent on the ground of accretion and the same were decreed. In or around 1942 one island char measuring 2.55 acres was formed out of the bed of the river opposite to CS Plot Nos. 51-54. A similar island char measuring 16.60 acres arose out of the bed of river Kazibacha. Both these island chars were surrounded on all sides by deep water of the river. Government under the provision of section 4 of Regulation No. XI/1825 claimed both the chars as khas land and the Collector of Khulna started Settlement Case No. 54/46-47, got both the chars surveyed and map prepared. Initially both these two chars, one situated to the south of the other, were allotted Touzi No. 1442 which was subsequently changed to Touzi No. 1444 under Khas Mahal Officer's Order dated 27.5.48. Defendant No. 2, Abdul Haque Sarder, Kali Kanta Chatterjee, Anil Kumar Ghosh and Bupendra Nath Das who were tenure holders under the aforesaid Touzi Nos. 120 and 1142 took permanent settlement in raiyati right of both the above mentioned island chars at a rental of rupees 3.00 per acre from the government on payment of salami and by executing 4 separate kabuliyats in the year 1946 AD. Kabuliyats were accepted by the government and the tenants paid rent. The kabuliyats contained the stipulation that in case of increment to the leased out island chars, the lessees would pay enhanced rent at the stipulated rate. Lessee Kali Kanta Chatterjee settled his share comprising 4.79 acres to defendant No. 3 Sk. Nuruddin by patta dated 10.2.48. Lessee Anil Kumar Ghosh sold his 4.79 acre to one Mahbubur Rahman who in turn settled 1.50 acres out of his purchased land with defendant Nos. 5-7 in 1354 BS at an annual rent at Rupees 7-8-0 annas and sold the remaining 3.29 acres as well as rent receiving interest of the settled 1.50 acres to defendant Nos. 5-7 by kabala dated 25.10.56. Bupendra Nath Das, the other lessee, sold his share to defendant No. 4 by kabala dated 20.12.48 while defendant No. 2 remained in possession of his share of leased land. Gradually further land accreted to the northern island char and defendant No. 2 began to possess that accreted land too. There are two khals or channels on the east and west of this char. Out of the land accreted to this char seven bighas was settled with Monsur Bawali and Sariatullah Sk. by patta dated 29.5.51 with an annual rent of Rupees 14-0-0 and they arc possessing that land. Defendant No. 2 is in possession of the landaccreted to this northern island char. Thus defendant No. 2 possessed 28.00 acres land including the tenanted land and Asli land of 2.55 acres of touzi No. 1444. He also possesses 2.23 acres on the eastern side of the southern char of touzi No. 1444 by virtue of his lease taken from the government and with gradual accretion to this land by the recess of the river he had been possessing the accreted land as well. Defendant No. 2 further alleges that before attachment of the land a proceeding under section 144 CrPC was started at the instance of the Khas Mahal Depart.ment wherein it was clearly admitted that the disputed land were accret.ion to touzi 120 and 1144 and the said proceeding was ultimately dropped. Defendant No. 2 further claims that before attachment by the Collect.or the char contiguous to CS Plot No. 3 was possessed by defendant No. 3 Dwarik Mondal who is korfatenant under one Nalini Bala Chatterjee who is an under-tenant under defendant No. 2, the tenure formed under CS Plot No. 47 was being possessed by successors of Bangeshwar Chatterjee; that the lands of block No. 1 of Collector's map was in possession of defendant No. 9 and sons of Bangeshwar; that the land accreted to CS Plot Nos. 8 and 9 was in possession of defendant No. 9 Rabia Khatun along with her co-sharers; the land accreted to CS Plot No. 101 was possessed by Upendra Nath Mondal and his co-sharers and these persons were tenants under defendant. No. 2 who realised additional rent for the additional areas; that one Zohura Khatun had been possessing CS Plots No. 113 and 115 of khatian No. 24 and portion of block Nos. 6 and 7 of Collector's map as accretion to her land by purchase from Satish Chandra Bhadra. Defendant No. 2 therefore prays for declaration of his title over the land accreted to touzi Nos. 1144 and 120, for recovery of possession which are now in possession of the receiver appointed by the Collector and for cost against the government. This defendant further made objections on formal points regarding maintainability of suit and correctness of the map attached to the letter of reference. 

 7. Defendant No.9 filed one written statement individually and another jointly with defendant Nos. 12-18. Their common case is that the disputed lands are accretions to the contiguous asli land and the owners of the said had been possessing the same as of right without any apprehension of breach of peace. Their further case is that defendant No. 2's predecessor Mofizuddin Sarder held the tenure recorded in khatian No. 7 of mouza Tetultala out of which defendant No. 9 and his brother Roopchand took settlement of four bighas at a rental of Rs. 2-8-0 annas per bigha by registered kabuJiyat dated 6th Ashar, 1326 BS which stood in the name of Roopchand and; that defendant No.9 and Roopchand then sold it to one Abdul Latif Khan, predecessor of Rabia Khatun and others, Abdul Latif then settled Ph bighas out of his land at a rental of Rs. 5.00 with defendant No. 9 Dwarik Mondal. Kazibacha river which previously flowed by the northern side of this land gradually receded towards further north as a result of which some additions were made to the aforesaid raiyati holding of Abdul Latif Khan and others which was recorded in CS Khatian No. 45. The Korfa jama of defendant No. 9 was recorded in Khatian No. 46. CS Plot No. 8 is within khas land of khatian No. 45 and CS Plot No. 9 is the khas land of CS Khatian No. 46. After CS operation river Kazibacha receded further north and about 40 bighas of land accreted to CS Plot Nos. 8 and 9. Due to this addition in the area landlord Abdul Haque Sarder i.e. defendant No. 2 of the present suit, brought Rent Suit No. 1676/1944 in the First Court of Munsif, Khulna claiming additional rent against Rabia Khatun and others which was decreed and the rent was increased from Rs. 10.00 to Rs. 75.00. By amicable arrangement defendant No. 9 possessed 3/8 share of this char land and the remaining 5/8 was being possessed by Rabia Khatun and others. The government claimed this land as island char and they have been dispossessed illegally from their land due to attachment by the Collector which was wrong. Defendant Nos. 9 and 12-18 therefore pray for declaration of their title, confirmation of possession and compensation. 

 11. Defendant Nos. 24 and 25 in their written statement state that at the time of CS operation river Kazibacha flowed by the eastern side of Jalma mouza and Tetultala mouza was to the east of the river. The river receded towards east and west causing diluviation of the same land but after some time such diluviated land reformed in situ. These reformed land have been wrongly recorded in Tetultala mouza. Some land of Jalma mouza is still under water of the river and then they were wrongly recorded as plot Nos. 83 and 91 of sheet No. 1 of mouza Tetultala in the CS map. Nanibala and other tenure holders locally known as 'gantidars' of Ja1ma mouza brought TS No. 5 of 1939 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Khulna praying for khas possession on declaration of their title. On transfer to the Court of Additional Subordinate Judge, Khulna the suit was renumbered as TS No. 20 of 1941. They obtained a decree in respect of plot Nos. 83 and 91 which reformed after CS operation and their claim for those lands which were recorded as the land of Tetultala in the CS map was dismissed. Nanibala and others in execution of the decree, took khas possession of the decretal land of the 2 plots and settled portions of the land with different tenants. In the map prepared by the Pleader Commissioner in Title Suit No. 20 of 1941 it was found that the land to the north of blocks 6 and 7 of the Collector's map is the land of Jalma mouza. During the pendency of the suit Kazibacha river receded towards north, south and west and the diluviated land of Jalma mouza gradually re-appeared in its original site. Thus according to these defendants the decretal land of Title Suit No. 20 of 1941 appeared as adjoining char thereby enabling its owner to possess it Defendant Nos. 24 and 25 took settlement of ten bighas and had been in possession till attachment by the Collector; that there were accretion to these land and these are covered by block Nos. 6 and 7 of the Collector's map. They pray for declaration of title, compensation and cost. 

 13. Defendant No. 27 also claims title on the basis of reformation in situ alleging that tenure holder Nanibala Devi and others brought Title Suit No. 5 of 1939 for recovery of possession on declaration of their title to these land. The suit on being renumbered as Title Suit No. 20 of 1941 was decreed in part with respect to those lands the claim of which was not barred by limitation. Thereafter Nanibala and others settled some of these lands of different persons and possessed the remaining land in khas. Block Nos. 6 and 7 of the Collector's map have been shown in that decree and the map as appertaining to the land of the said tenants. Further case of defendant No. 27 is that during the pendency of that suit river Kazibacha receded towards north, south and west causing diluvian of some land of Jalma mouza but subsequently those lands re-appeared in the situ and formed the char land which were the decretal land of that suit. Nanibala and others possessed that land. Thereafter defendant No. 27 took lease of eight bighas from Nanibala by registered kabuliyat dated 24.9.42. Where after more accretion took place on the south of these lands and defendant No. 27 possessed them till the date of attachment by the Collector. The said accreted land of defendant No. 27 are identical with block Nos. 6 and 7 of the Collector's map. He also claims 

 Defendant Nos. 31-37 after alleging defect in the form of the reference, incorrectness of the map prepared by the Collector and non-service of notice upon them, allege that they filed Title Suit No. 168 of 1949 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Khulna which was transferred to the Court of Munsifs Court, Khulna and renumbered as Title Suit No. 155 of 1951. In that suit they claimed a portion of the disputed land and the parties in the present proceeding also claiming the same land in that suit and in that circumstances the present Proceeding being Title Suit No. 5 of 1969 should be stayed. Their further case is that the land of block Nos. 1-3 of the Collector's map and land adjoining to these 3 blocks appertain to mauza Rangiamari of touzi No. 188 the proprietor of which was Syedpur Trust Estate. The Lahiris held a pattani of which 5 gandas share belonged to Bijoy Lal Lahiri and the remaining 15 annas 15 gandas to Nirode Bashini Mitra and Hemanta Kumar Ghosh and it was recorded in CS Khatian No. 2 of the mouza. Nirode Bashini held a Mourashi Jama under Bijoy Lal which was recorded in CS Khatian No. 3. Bijoy Kumar Das. Srcepati Nath and others held a Darpattani under the said pattani and it was recorded in CS khatian No. 4. Chandra Kanta Dcv held an ejara under Sreepati in half share of her darpattani which was recorded in CS khatian No. 2. Under this ejara and under Bijoy's 8 annas of darpattani Srimanta Chatterjce, Charu Mitra and others held a ganti (tenure) which was recorded in CS khatian No. 32 and under this ganti, there was a darganti which devolved on Soroju Bala Hari recorded in CS khatian No. 33. One Goura Mohan Patrabanik held a Mourashi Abadi Ganti under this darganti which was auction purchased in a rent sale on 9-8-50 by one Pran Hari Das in the benami of Matura Guha. The heirs of Pran Hari sold the ganti to Surja Kumar Khasnabish and Shashi Kumar Banarjee by kabala dated 8.11.1906 which was subsequently purchased by Bagcshwar and his brother Raijeshwar Banarjee in a rent sale and took possession. The land of plot Nos. 1-3 and their adjoining lands appeartain to the said ganti of Goura Mohan Patrabanik. Some of these land were wrongly recorded in the names of trespassers in CS records of Tetultala and CS Khaitian No. 166 of mouza Raingamari. At the time of creation of this ganti Kazibacha river was flowing by the south and east of mouza Rangiamari and Tetultala was to the east of this ganti. The river then receded towards south, north and west as a result of which major portion of the said ganti was diluviated but afterwards it reformed in situ and were attached to Tetultala mouza wrongly. CS Dag No. 92 of Tetultana and CS Dag No. 1025 of Rangimari which were recorded as river are actually the land of the said ganti which were auction purchased by Bhaigeshwar Biswas. After CS operation Kazibacha river receded further north and more land accreted to plot Nos. 1-4, 7-10. 12, 27, 93, 124, 79 and 101 and other adjoining land of mouza Tetultala. These land as shown in block Nos. 1-3 of the Collector's map and the adjoining land actually appertained to mouza Rangimari included in the ganti which was auction-purchased by Bhaigeshwar Biswas. CS Plot Nos. 935-937, 1022 and 1023 were wrongly recorded in the name of Nasim Shaik and others under the said ganti though they never possessed the same. These plots and other khan lands of the ganti were diluviated but sometime after they reformed in situ to the southern side of the ganti. Claimant Nos. 1-3, 6-8 and father of claimant Nos. 4 and 5 took permanent lease of about 49.88 acres or 100 bighas as per local measurement from Bhaigeshwar and Rajeshwar Biswas by a patta dated 13th Falgoon, 1354 BS in the name of Abdul Haque, Usha Rani Dashi and Anna Puma Devi. The land of this patta are contiguous to the north of CS Plot Nos. 1-4, 6-9, 12, 27, 93 and 101 of mouza Tetultala, they appertain to Bhaighadhar's ganti which reformed in situ and are identical with the land shown in block Nos. 1-3 of the Collector's map. 

 Thus the law as it was in force at the relevant time provided that all alluvial land would be increment to the land of the Zaminder or tenant who held the main land under any superior landlord including the government. No doubt in the third clause it has been provided that if a char is thrown opened in a large navigable river the bed of which is not the property of any individual and if the channels of the river between the char and the main land are not fordable it shall be at the disposal of the government, but if the channel is fordable in any season of the year it shall be acquisition to the land of the persons whose estate may be most contiguous to it. Relying on this provision of law, the leaned Deputy Attorney-General Mr. Moazzem Hossain contends that it is admitted by almost all the contending parties in the suit that two island chars arose out of the bed of the river Kazibacha which was navigable at the relevant time and the two chars have been depicted as 'A' in the sketch map, in that view of the matter, according to him, these two chars belong to the government as per provision of clause (3) of section 4 of regulation XI of 1825 and any accretion to these two chars are accretion to government khas land and no one else can set forth claim over them. There is no doubt about the fact that PWs 1 and 2 as well as OWs 1-6 who were witnesses for defendant Nos. 2-7 in unequivocal language stated that in or around 1940 two island chars, one described as the northern char comprising of 2.55 acres, and the other as the southern char comprising 16.60 acres arose out of the bed of the river Kazibacha running through mouza Tetultala. DW 8 Mansur Bawali who is defendant No. 22, DW 9 Hatem Ahmed who deposed on behalf of defendant Nos. 9 and 12-18, DW 10 Tarek Mondal who deposed on behalf of defendant No. 21 also supported the case of the government and DWs 1-6 about the raising of these two chars out of the bed of the river which belonged to nobody. Therefore, there remains no doubt about the fact that immediately after the formation of these two island chars marked 'A' in the sketch map, those were at the disposal of the government. But it is the case of the defendant No. 2 and others that he, Kali Kanta Chatterjee, Anil Kumar Ghosh and Bhupendra Nath Das took lease of both the Chars in their totality from the government by executing four kabuliyats. The kabuliyat executed by Kali Kanta Chaterjee has not been produced in Court as because in spite of being called for the government who is supposed to be in custody of the same, did not file it. But the other three kabuliyats executed in the year 1946 have been filed in Court and marked as A, A(1) and A(2). These three documents prove that defendant Abdul Haque Sarker, Anil Kumar Ghosh and Bhupendra Nath Das executed kabuliyat in favour of the government for 4.79 acres of land each of the two island chars. Mr. Moazzem Hossain tried to argue that mere execution of the kabuliyats cannot create tenancy in favour of these executants unless the same were accepted by the government and the executants were recognised as tenants. But the documents Ext. A, A(I) and A(2) show that these were accepted by Khas Mohal Officer, Khulna and the said Officer also attested the same as witness. Moreover, these sets of defendants filed series of dakhilas to prove that they paid rent to the government for their leased land. So there cannot be any doubt about the fact that the two chars after becoming cultivable, were leased out by the government to defendant No. 1 Abdul Haque Sarder, Kali Kanta Chatterjee, Haran Kumar Ghosh and Bhupendra Nath Das in 1946 and subsequently rent was also accepted from them. With the leasing out of the land these four persons became tenure holders under the government and therefore on and from date of their acquisition of lease hold right over the two island chars clause (1) of section 4 of Regulation XI of 1825 became operative and by virtue of that provision of law they became entitled to anyadditional land which was gained to the two original island chars by recession of the river as increment to their tenure. Under the circumstances the plea taken by the government that since the two original chars marked 'A' in the Collector's sketch map, belonged to the government any accretion to them would automatically vest in the government is unacceptable. These accretions by operation of law as was in force at the time of such accretion, went to the tenure holders and their under tenants as well as the transferees as increment to their holdings. Of course, if the other set of defendants namely defendant Nos. 24-25, 26, 27, 30, 31-37 and 38-39 could show that these newly risen lands were reformation in situ of their land which previously were diluviated, then their claim would get preference. The documents filed in the trial Court show that by Ext. B one of the lease holders Kali Kanta Chatterjee, leased out his share to defendant No. 3, Sk. Nuruddin, that defendant No. 4, Emdad Ali Khan purchased the share for Buhpendra by kabala Ext. F and one Mahbubur Rahman purchased this interest of Anil Kumar by Ext. F(2) who in turn sold it to defendant Nos. 5-7 by Ext. F(1). These persons possessed their respective land in the islands and paid rent to the government and obtained dakhilas marked Ext. B series. The sketch map also shows that the accreted lands which are subject matter of the dispute depicted as blocks 1 to 5, surround the original northern island char of 2.55 acres while block Nos. 6 and 7 are contiguous to original southern island char of 16.60 acres and those have been attached by the Collector, being subject matter of contention between the parties and cause of apprehension of breach of peace. It may also be mentioned here that the kabuliyats marked Ext. A to A(2) contained the stipulation that in case of increase in the area of four lease hold lands the lessees would be liable to pay increased rent. This stipulation in other words means that the lessees would be entitled to any accretion that may happen to the areas of the original leased out land. In the Collector's map two khals or channels have been shown, one running between the block Nos. 2 and 3 and the other one between the block Nos. 6 and 7. PW 1, the District Kanungo tried to make out a case that these khals were navigable but he could not give the exact depth of the khals and on the other hand, he admitted that he had no personal knowledge of the origin of the khals or if they were fordable or not. On the other hand, DW 1 categorically stated that the khals were fordable at the time of formation of the disputed chars and that subsequently those have further silted up. Defendant Nos. 2-11, 12-18 and 21 and 23 claimed the disputed land as accretion to their tenancies. It. has been already stated that kabuliyats dated 18-10-46, 6-9-49 and 26.5.46 show that 4.79 acre of lands were taken settlement by each of DW 1 Abdul Haque Sarder, Kali Kanta Chatterjee and Anil 

 Kanta Ghosh at a rental of Rs. 3.00 per acre. It has also been shown that defendant Nos. 3-7 acquired the interest of Kali Kanta, Anil Ghosh and Bhupcn Das. Defendant No. 2 Abdul Haque Sarker claims 2.55 acres in the northern island and 2.23 acres in the southern island and also 28.00 acres as accretion to his original leased land. Out of these lands he has let out some to tenants who are parties in the suit and who support him. On the other hand, defendant Nos. 24-39 claim reformation in situ. Defendant Nos. 24-27 claim that disputed land originally were in mouza Jalma which was to the west of river Kazibacha while Tetultala was on the east, that during CS operation the river receded towards the north, south and was causing diluvion of some land of Jalma. Their further case is that the diluviated land subsequently re-appeared in their original sites, that Nanibala and others were tenure holders of mouza Jalma and on reformation these tenure holders brought Title Suit No. 5 of 1939 which was subsequently renumbered as 20/41 for the recovery of khas possession of these re-appeared land and obtained part decree in respect of the land described in schedule "kha" to the plaint of that suit and that their claim with respect to schedule "Ka" was dismissed. Their further case is that after obtaining decree these tenure holders settled the land with different tenants including defendant Nos. 24-27. So the sheet anchor of the claim of the these defendants is the decree obtained by their superior landlords in TS No. 20 of 1941. Admittedly the suit was with respect to the land of Jalma. But these defendants in the present suit did not take any attempt to relay the map attached to the decree passed in TS No. 20/41 in order to ascertain that the decretal land of that suit are identical with any portion of the present disputed land as shown in blocks No. 1-7 of the Collector's map. There is no dispute about the fact that in the CS map the whole of the river Kazibacha was included within mouza Tetultala while the eastern boundary line of both Jalma and Rangiamari was the western bank of the river. It is also not disputed that even after the change of course of the river there runs a channel in between the accreted land and the two villages Jalma and Rangiamari. Therefore, without relying the connected village maps it cannot be said that the disputed land are contiguous part of village Jalma and Rangiamari or that these char lands have re-appeared in the old sites which were originally depicted as part of Jalma or Rangiamari. Moreover, in Title Suit No. 20 of 1941 the government and some of the present claimants were not made parties and as such the decree passed in that suit is not binding upon them. Defendant No. 30 as DW 14 claims possession over the land. But from his deposition it transpires that he has no idea about the land and has no paper to show his possession. In that view of the matter, the trial Court has rightly held that the document Ext.A(9) is a spurious one. Defendant Nos. 31-37 claim 49.88 acres under the patta dated 13th Falgoon, 1354 BS marked Ext. A(7) purported to have been executed by Bhaigyadhar and Rajeshwar. The identity of this land has not been established by relaying the map. The Pleader Commissioner DW 18 said that he visited the land but in the next breath he said that plot No. 101 was under water at the time of his visit. On scrutiny of his deposition it appears that this Commissioner prepared his report Exts B(7) and C(7) sitting in his house without visiting the locality. Moreover, the map and the report in question were prepared by him in connection with Title Suit No. 155 of 1951 which suit is still pending and the report and the map of the Commissioner have not been accepted by the Court as yet. Kiran Biswas as DW 13 claimed that up to Kartick, 1355 BS Bhaigyadhar and defendant Nos. 31-37 possessed the land but could not produce any documentary evidence to substantiate his contention. He did not know if defendant Nos. 2, 3 and others took settlement of the land from government by executing four kabuliyats. Again, in a proceeding under section 145 CrPC this very witness claimed some land appertaining to mouza Tetultala. Thus he himself destroyed his credibility by saying one thing at one time and another at another time. Moreover, these defendants also did not take any step to get the land surveyed for the purpose of establishing their identity. Amrit Lal Guha who is said to have cultivated the land from 1362 BS has not been produced as witness. Moreover, DW 13 could not say who possessed plot Nos. 1009, 1015, 1045 and 1046 of block No. 2. From his cross-examination it transpires that the land of Rangiamari mouza is still under water and the entire land of block Nos. 1, 2 and 3 do not appeartain to that mouza. So he has virtually destroyed the case of this defendant that these three blocks reformed in the old situ and appertaining to Rangiamari mouza. Defendant Nos. 38 and 39 also did not give sufficient description of their land in their written statement. Defendant No.
